sources.name: English Wiktionary translations via Kaikki/Wiktextract
sources.attribution: Wiktionary contributors; extracted by Wiktextract/Kaikki (Tatu Ylonen and contributors). Sense selection, filtering, and topic assignments by Jenechka Cards.
sources.methodology: Handselected exact translation-table meanings and source parts of speech, with explicit sourced preferences and exclusions in scripts/fetch-lexicon.py. Source grammar, register, and regional tags are retained. Chinese paired spellings and three explicitly normalized annotation fields retain their full sourceText. English studyText qualifiers distinguish selected homographs. Missing or uncertain translations stay missing. This dictionary-derived seed is not native-speaker reviewed, not a frequency list, and carries no CEFR assignments. Source POS describes the selected English dictionary sense; it is not a separately verified POS classification for every target-language form. Arabic verbs may use dictionary third-person perfect forms; some Asian adjective forms are attributive. The checked-in JSON freezes the selected forms and exact meaning/POS/source hash; rebuilding rejects changed source hashes unless --refresh is requested. Additional topic/context assignments use individual dictionary-sense review by the coding assistant. This model-assisted semantic curation is recorded by exact concept ID, meaning and POS in source-data/topic-supplement.json and source-data/context-supplement.json; it is not native-speaker review.
sources.version: Single-word source snapshots retrieved 2026-10-20; SHA-256 recorded for each concept

sources.name: FrequencyWords — OpenSubtitles 2018
sources.attribution: FrequencyWords by Hermit Dave; derived from OPUS OpenSubtitles 2018 and OpenSubtitles.org. Content is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0. Jenechka Cards extracts the first 1,000 original rows per language and converts them to JSON without changing their order or counts.
sources.methodology: Original corpus token counts, not lemma or sense frequencies. rank is the one-based upstream row number. Punctuation, fragments, foreign words, and inflected forms are deliberately retained; nothing is filtered, normalized, lemmatized, or re-ranked here. Chinese uses zh_cn; Portuguese uses pt, not pt_br. These data do not establish CEFR levels or verified translations. A downstream lexicon match must preserve the original rank and report partial coverage instead of relabeling a subset as a complete Top N deck. Only dictionary-matched forms are used in this app. Original ranks are not renumbered. Matching ignores case, Russian stress marks, and optional Arabic vowel marks; it does not stem words, aggregate inflections, or transfer ranks between languages.

sources.name: CEFR-J Wordlist Version 1.6
sources.license: CEFR-J attribution permission; research, educational and commercial use permitted
sources.attribution: The CEFR-J Wordlist Version 1.6. Compiled by Yukio Tono, Tokyo University of Foreign Studies. Copyright Tono Laboratory, TUFS. Retrieved from https://www.cefr-j.org/data/CEFRJ_wordlist_ver1.6.zip on 20/10/2026. Normalized and filtered for Jenechka Cards; source labels retained.
sources.methodology: English textbook corpora graded by CEFR-J, supplemented against the English Vocabulary Profile. Classification is for headword and part of speech, not individually verified senses. Use ALL; split slash alternatives only when every resulting form is explicitly present with the same POS and level in the official ALL_sep sheet. Exclude conflicting lemma/POS levels. No level is inferred from frequency or transferred to another language.

sources.name: SMARTool data for English-speaking learners of Russian
sources.attribution: SMARTool dataset by Radovan Bast, Laura A. Janda, Mikhail Kopotev, Olga Lyashevskaya, James D. McDonald, Tore Nesset, Ekaterina Rakhilina, Svetlana Sokolova, Evgeniia Sudarikova, Francis M. Tyers, Valentina Zhukova, and Elizaveta Kibisova. https://doi.org/10.18710/QNAPNE. CC BY 4.0. Source CSVs normalized, grouped and filtered for Jenechka Cards; no endorsement implied.
sources.methodology: Russian lexemes selected from textbooks and CEFR lexical minima by experienced teachers at three universities. Retain supplied A1-B2 labels and English glosses, which may contain alternatives or usage context; do not claim these are separately validated sense-level CEFR annotations. Exclude missing fields, editorial artifacts, file/row level conflicts and any lemma/POS/gloss combination with conflicting levels. Group repeated wordform/example rows by normalized lemma, coarse POS and exact normalized gloss. Remove combining acute stress marks but preserve ё and й. Map N.* to noun, A to adjective and V to verb. Topics are exact English labels from the pinned source Topics.csv; composite labels remain composite. Never reuse Russian CEFR labels for English.

sources.name: Octanove English Vocabulary Profile C1–C2 1.0
sources.attribution: Octanove Labs; distributed by Open Language Profiles.
sources.methodology: Source-assigned English C1/C2 headword and part-of-speech classifications, joined only to exact English dictionary lemma/POS matches. Conflicting levels and unmatched POS are omitted. These are the publisher's supplementary classifications, not official CEFR certification of individual dictionary senses. No classification is transferred to translations or other languages.

sources.name: Intercontinental Dictionary Series (IDS)
sources.attribution: Key, Mary Ritchie & Comrie, Bernard (eds.) 2023. The Intercontinental Dictionary Series. Leipzig: Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology. CLDF v4.4, DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23245041. Digitization: Robert Forkel, Christoph Rzymski, Hans-Jörg Bibiko and contributors. Dictionary authors: Italian: Martin Maiden; French: various; Spanish: Joan Rafel;various; Portuguese: various; English: various; Dutch: Bernard Bichakjian;Hendrikje Hettema; German: Meredith Lee.
sources.methodology: Concepts and semantic chapters copied from IDS. Existing equivalent animal/food/time/communication categories are reused; additional narrow and contextual categories use explicit, manually reviewed IDS concept IDs. Current English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese and Dutch dictionaries; Spanish forms require an exact standard Spanish Wiktionary headword match. One first accepted source form per language/concept is selected; additional synonyms remain research evidence and are not automatically presented as equivalent study answers. Parenthetically qualified groups and usage/region/POS-qualified groups are omitted conservatively. NFC normalization preserves accents; no transliteration, translation generation, frequency or CEFR assignment. Six observed German capitalization/POS mismatches are excluded explicitly rather than silently corrected. Russian IDS uses Latin phonemic transcription with information loss and is excluded. POS is retained only where the source concept explicitly labels it; unspecified is not inferred. IDS is a comparative dictionary with broad concept groupings and historical lexicographic origins, not an exhaustive modern learner curriculum or native-speaker review.

sources.name: Spanish Wiktionary headwords via Kaikki (IDS spelling validation)
sources.attribution: Wiktionary contributors; extracted by Wiktextract/Kaikki (Tatu Ylonen and contributors). Used to check exact Spanish headword spellings against IDS candidates.
sources.methodology: Exact NFC headword matching, preserving case and accents. At least one ordinary non-form-of sense must be present; entries supported only by obsolete, archaic, nonstandard or spelling-error senses are excluded. No meanings or CEFR labels are transferred from this validation source and IPA is never converted to spelling.
sources.version: Kaikki postprocessed Spanish, enwiktionary dump 2026-09-02; extraction 2026-10-03

sources.name: English Wiktionary sense-aligned translation tables via Kaikki/Wiktextract
sources.attribution: Wiktionary contributors; extracted by Wiktextract/Kaikki (Tatu Ylonen and contributors). Subset extraction, standard-language filtering, equivalent selection and English sense labels by Jenechka Cards.
sources.methodology: A concept retains one explicit English POS/etymology/translation-table meaning. Both entry-level and nested sense-level translations are read. Selection uses existing English source headword inventories (CEFR-J and the supplemental levels.json) or exact target-language top-1000 native token matches; it does not assign CEFR or transfer frequency ranks. Foreign forms are literal source translations in that exact table. Standard-language/register filters reject unknown tags, dialects, malformed annotations and unexpected script. Equivalent selection within one table prefers unqualified standard forms, then the equivalent's own-language original corpus rank, then source order. Selected tags and other eligible variants remain in the source artifact. English study sides include the exact translation heading to distinguish senses. Categories use topics of explicit parent source senses (categoryAssociation=source-parent-sense), or an exact translation heading-to-gloss/sense-id match (exact-gloss-or-sense-id); otherwise they are unassigned. Parent-sense associations are Kaikki postprocessing, not a new human disambiguation claim. Existing hand-reviewed sense keys are omitted. The shared English source POS is not independently verified as the grammatical class of every translation. No SMARTool links are inferred. Automatically extracted dictionary data, not native-speaker reviewed. Additional topic/context assignments use individual dictionary-sense review by the coding assistant. This model-assisted semantic curation is recorded by exact concept ID, meaning and POS in source-data/topic-supplement.json and source-data/context-supplement.json; it is not native-speaker review. Raw parent-sense topic labels are not trusted by nesting alone: automatic topic assignment requires an exact normalized translation-heading/gloss match; other topics require individual sense review. Reviewed corrections/exclusions are recorded in source-data/form-review.json and quality-*.json. Corrections distinguish same-sense source alternatives, notation cleanup and editorial repairs. All forms undergo structural screening; this does not certify every meaning as independently native-reviewed. Parenthetical annotations and readings are omitted from study faces while source metadata is retained.

sources.name: CC-CEDICT Chinese–English Dictionary
sources.attribution: CC-CEDICT contributors, published by MDBG; original CEDICT by Paul Andrew Denisowski.
sources.methodology: Dictionary-derived English glosses are definitions, not independently sourced English entries. Corpus selection uses real dictionary lemmata with exact NFC/casefold token matches; Arabic matching additionally removes vowel marks and tatweel while retaining hamza. Original FrequencyWords token ranks are preserved, never treated as sense or lemma frequencies. At most 1800 matched lemmata per language and 2 senses per lemma, preferring unmarked usage over literary/colloquial/slang tags. Japanese additionally includes at most 150 verbs, 100 adjectives, and 50 adverbs with explicit JMdict common-priority codes and no invented frequency match. No inferred CEFR/HSK/JLPT/TOPIK levels or machine translations. Not native-speaker reviewed. English gloss identity alone does not establish equivalence with another dictionary sense. Simplified forms and individual slash-delimited glosses copied from CC-CEDICT. Proper names, reference-only/used-in glosses, bound forms, explicitly archaic/literary/dialectal definitions, classifier lists, and long definitions excluded. Source register annotations are preserved as tags. CC-CEDICT does not provide POS; unknown is retained rather than guessed.

sources.name: Jenechka modern vocabulary and corrections
sources.attribution: Jenechka Cards contributors; original model-assisted editorial translations and corrections.
sources.methodology: Original everyday vocabulary with one defined meaning per row and translations in all thirteen languages. Model-assisted editorial additions and repairs are distinguished from dictionary-attested alternatives. No proprietary learning-app vocabulary was used; independent native-speaker certification is not claimed.

sources.name: Jenechka editorial level estimates
sources.attribution: Jenechka Cards contributors; model-assisted editorial study-band estimates.
sources.methodology: Estimated, not official or independently validated CEFR levels. Native-language editorial anchors take precedence; other estimates combine native subtitle familiarity with meaning/domain, part of speech, register and language-specific lexical complexity. Frequency is never the only input. Unknown corpus frequency is treated as missing evidence, not proof of advanced difficulty. Published English CEFR-J/Octanove and Russian SMARTool assignments are retained separately. No English level is transferred to another language and no HSK/JLPT/TOPIK-to-CEFR equivalence is asserted. Each entry belongs to one band; contextual polysemy can change learning difficulty.

limitations: This is a partial dictionary-derived library, not a complete multilingual curriculum.
Wiktionary translation senses were selected and filtered; not every form has independent native-speaker review.
The shared dictionary POS describes the source concept, not independently verified target-language grammar.
Frequency uses raw subtitle word forms, not lemma frequencies; unmatched tokens and missing translations are omitted without filling lower ranks.
English CEFR-J/Octanove and Russian SMARTool labels are headword/POS classifications, not certified sense levels. Remaining labels are explicitly estimated using a native-language editorial rubric.
Monolingual dictionary English glosses are translations only; no automatic translation, cross-dictionary sense guessing, or English fallback is used.
